title: Futures Contract Fundamentals: Standardization, Mechanics, and Convergence
prerequisites: Basic understanding of spot markets and standard buy/sell order types
learningOutcomes: Differentiate between long and short futures positions and calculate their respective profits and losses
Identify the core standardized elements of commodity, financial, and index futures contracts
Explain the role of daily price limits and speculative position limits enforced by exchanges
Describe the convergence mechanism of futures prices toward spot prices and evaluate the structural role of physical delivery

sections.title: Futures Foundations and Position Mechanics
keyPoints: Explores the standardized structure of futures contracts and the core mechanics of entering long or short positions.

sections.title: Contract Specifications Across Asset Classes
keyPoints: Details standardized contract parameters across agricultural, debt, and index instruments, including grading differentials and multipliers.

sections.title: Exchange Governance: Volatility and Exposure Limits
keyPoints: Covers regulatory safeguards including daily price limits (limit up/down) and speculative position limits.

sections.title: Delivery Mechanics and Price Convergence
keyPoints: Examines the convergence of futures prices to spot prices and the real-world implications of delivery obligations.

misconceptions.misconception: Futures trading routinely forces speculators to receive truckloads of physical commodities upon expiration.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Physical delivery occurs in less than 1% of transactions; participants virtually always close positions before the delivery cycle, though the mere potential for delivery anchors market pricing.

misconceptions.misconception: Futures prices can swing infinitely in a single trading session during extreme panic or euphoria.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Exchanges institute daily price limits (limit up and limit down) that halt or restrict trading beyond predefined bands to curb speculative volatility.

activeRecallQuiz.scenario: A trader accidentally holds 2 CME Live Cattle contracts into delivery instead of closing them. What physical burden do they face, and why did futures prices converge to spot right before this occurred?
activeRecallQuiz.question: A trader accidentally holds 2 CME Live Cattle contracts into delivery instead of closing them. What physical burden do they face, and why did futures prices converge to spot right before this occurred?
activeRecallQuiz.correctAnswer: Correctly identifying the downside risk and margin constraints.
activeRecallQuiz.explanation: Holding 2 CME Live Cattle contracts creates an obligation for 80,000 lbs of physical cattle requiring transit and care ([fact-07]). As the delivery month approaches, arbitrage and delivery mechanisms force the futures price to converge toward the spot price ([fact-04], [fact-10]).

coreTakeaways: Futures contracts are exchange-traded, standardized instruments where longs agree to buy and shorts agree to sell at a set price and future date.
Contract size, deliverable grade premiums/discounts, and multipliers vary strictly by contract specification.
Even though physical delivery occurs in under 1% of trades, its threat enforces price convergence (F_T ≈ S_T) through arbitrage.
